cases.translation: The time had come, she fell in love
cases.explain: Пора is the grammatical subject of пришла (had come), so it stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: у ___ любовницы прекрасной мне приходили на язык
cases.translation: At the feet of my beautiful mistress they used to come to my tongue
cases.explain: The preposition у (at) governs the genitive plural, so ноги becomes ног.

cases.sentence: пошли тихонько внука с запиской этой к ___
cases.translation: Quietly send the grandson with this note to the neighbor
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) always requires the dative case, so сосед becomes соседу.

cases.translation: Give me a pen and paper, nanny
cases.explain: Бумагу is the direct object of the imperative дай (give), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: And she goes into the garden to grieve
cases.explain: The preposition в expressing motion into a place governs the accusative, so сад stays сад (inanimate accusative = nominative form).

cases.sentence: на столик ставят вощиной кувшин с брусничной ___
cases.translation: They set a waxed pitcher of lingonberry water on the little table
cases.explain: The preposition с meaning 'with' governs the instrumental case, so вода becomes водой.

cases.sentence: В саду служанки на грядах сбирали ягоды в ___
cases.translation: In the garden the maidservants on the beds were gathering berries among the bushes
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating static location requires the prepositional plural, so кусты becomes кустах.

cases.translation: She brings tea on a tray
cases.explain: The preposition на indicating a static surface requires the prepositional case, so поднос becomes подносе.

reading.question: What is Onegin's teasing reaction to Lensky's plans?
options: He mockingly sighs, 'Oh, these poets of mine'
He asks to come along immediately
reading.correct: He mockingly sighs, 'Oh, these poets of mine'
reading.explain: Onegin teases Lensky with 'Where to? Oh, these poets of mine,' mocking his romantic eagerness.

reading.question: Where does Lensky say he spends every evening, prompting Onegin's surprise?
reading.correct: At the Larins' house
reading.explain: Lensky answers 'At the Larins',' and Onegin remarks 'how wonderful' in surprise.

reading.ru: Простая русская семья, К гостям усердие большое, Варенье и вечный разговор Про дождь, про день, про скотный двор.
reading.question: How does Onegin describe the Larin household to Lensky?
options: A simple Russian family, eager hospitality, jam, and endless talk of weather and the farmyard
A wealthy aristocratic salon full of intellectuals
A foreign household that speaks only French
An empty house with no one living there
reading.correct: A simple Russian family, eager hospitality, jam, and endless talk of weather and the farmyard
reading.explain: Onegin sums up the Larins as a simple family with great hospitality and conversation about rain, the day, and the farmyard.

reading.ru: Несут на блюдечках варенье, на столик ставят вощиной кувшин с брусничной водой.
reading.question: What refreshments are served to the young men at the Larins'?
options: Jam on little saucers and a pitcher of lingonberry water
reading.correct: Jam on little saucers and a pitcher of lingonberry water
reading.explain: The text describes jam brought on saucers and a waxed pitcher of lingonberry water set on the table.

reading.question: What does Onegin ask Lensky as they ride home?
options: Which of the sisters is Tatiana
Where the Larins' estate is located
When the wedding will take place
reading.correct: Which of the sisters is Tatiana
reading.explain: Onegin asks Lensky directly, 'Tell me, which one is Tatiana?'

reading.question: What surprised question does Onegin ask Lensky about Olga?
options: Whether he is really in love with the younger sister
Whether he plans to marry the elder sister
Whether he has ever met Olga before
Whether Olga is older than Tatiana
reading.correct: Whether he is really in love with the younger sister
reading.explain: Onegin teases, 'Can it be you're in love with the younger one?' referring to Olga.

reading.ru: Меж тем Онегина явление у Ларина произвело на всех большое впечатление и всех соседей развлекло.
reading.question: What effect did Onegin's appearance at the Larins' have on the neighborhood?
options: It made a big impression on everyone and amused all the neighbors
It frightened all the guests away
It caused a public scandal immediately
reading.correct: It made a big impression on everyone and amused all the neighbors
reading.explain: The text says Onegin's appearance at the Larins' 'made a big impression on everyone and amused all the neighbors.'

reading.question: What gossip do the neighbors start about Tatiana?
options: They start predicting/matching a bridegroom for Tatiana
They claim she is moving to Moscow
They say she refuses all visitors
reading.correct: They start predicting/matching a bridegroom for Tatiana
reading.explain: The gossip includes 'predicting a bridegroom for Tatiana,' assuming Onegin's interest.

reading.question: What happens to Tatiana as a result of hearing all this gossip and meeting Onegin?
options: Her time had come, and she fell in love
She grew angry at her mother
reading.correct: Her time had come, and she fell in love
reading.explain: The narrator states plainly: 'The time had come, she fell in love.'

reading.ru: Увы, теперь и дни, и ночи, и жаркий одинокий сон, все полно им.
reading.question: How completely does Onegin now occupy Tatiana's thoughts?
options: Her days, nights, and even her lonely dreams are all full of him
She thinks of him only occasionally
She thinks only of Lensky instead
reading.correct: Her days, nights, and even her lonely dreams are all full of him
reading.explain: The text says her days, nights, and even her hot lonely sleep are 'all full of him.'

reading.ru: Теперь с каким она вниманием читает сладостный роман
reading.question: How does Tatiana now read her sentimental novels?
reading.correct: With intense, absorbed attention
reading.explain: The text asks with what attention she now reads a sweet novel, showing her rapt absorption.

reading.ru: Но наш герой, кто б ни был он, уж верно был не Грандисон.
reading.question: How does the narrator contrast Onegin with the fictional hero Grandison?
options: He assures us Onegin was certainly not a Grandison
He claims Onegin was exactly like Grandison
He says Onegin had never heard of Grandison
He compares Onegin favorably to Grandison
reading.correct: He assures us Onegin was certainly not a Grandison
reading.explain: The narrator notes that whoever our hero really was, 'he certainly was not a Grandison,' the idealized novel hero.

reading.ru: Татьяна, милая Татьяна, с тобой теперь я слезы лью.
reading.question: How does the narrator express his feelings toward Tatiana at this point?
options: He says he now sheds tears together with her
He says he feels nothing for her
He blames her for her own troubles
reading.correct: He says he now sheds tears together with her
reading.explain: The narrator addresses her directly: 'Tatiana, dear Tatiana, with you now I shed tears.'

reading.ru: Тоска любви Татьяну гонит, И в сад идет она грустить.
reading.question: What drives Tatiana out into the garden?
reading.correct: The anguish of love
reading.explain: The text says 'the anguish of love drives Tatiana, and she goes into the garden to grieve.'

reading.ru: Татьяна в темноте не спит и тихо с няней говорит.
reading.question: What does Tatiana do at night instead of sleeping?
options: She quietly talks with her nanny
She writes letters to Onegin immediately
reading.correct: She quietly talks with her nanny
reading.explain: The text says 'Tatiana does not sleep in the dark, and quietly talks with her nanny.'

reading.ru: Да как же ты венчалась, няня?
reading.question: What does Tatiana ask her old nanny about?
options: What the nanny's parents were like
Whether the nanny ever loved a poet
reading.correct: How the nanny got married
reading.explain: Tatiana asks her nanny, 'But how did you get married, nanny?'

reading.question: What does Tatiana finally confess to her nanny?
options: That she wants to leave home
reading.correct: That she is in love
reading.explain: Tatiana confesses directly, 'You know, nanny, I am in love.'

reading.question: What does Tatiana ask her nanny to bring her?
reading.correct: A pen and paper
reading.explain: Tatiana asks, 'Give me, nanny, a pen and paper,' intending to write her letter.

reading.question: What has Tatiana finished by dawn?
options: Her letter is ready and folded
A new dress she was sewing
reading.correct: Her letter is ready and folded
reading.explain: The text states plainly, 'The letter is ready, folded.'

reading.ru: Я к вам пишу, чего же боли?
reading.question: How does Tatiana's letter to Onegin begin?
options: "I am writing to you, what more is there to say?"
"I hate you and never wish to see you"
reading.correct: "I am writing to you, what more is there to say?"
reading.explain: Tatiana's letter opens with 'I am writing to you, what more is there [to say]?'

reading.question: What does Tatiana claim in her letter about how she first knew Onegin?
options: That he had appeared to her in dreams
That her mother had described him in detail
That she had read about him in a novel
That Lensky had introduced them formally
reading.correct: That he had appeared to her in dreams
reading.explain: Her letter says 'you appeared to me in my dreams' even before they met.

reading.question: How does Tatiana behave after finishing and sealing her letter?
options: She alternately sighs and moans in anxiety
reading.correct: She alternately sighs and moans in anxiety
reading.explain: The text says 'Tatiana now sighs, now moans,' showing her nervous agitation.

reading.question: Who arrives at the Larin house while Tatiana anxiously awaits a reply?
reading.correct: Olga's admirer (Lensky)
reading.explain: The text announces 'Olga's admirer has arrived,' meaning Lensky.

reading.question: What sudden sound startles and terrifies Tatiana?
reading.correct: The sound of hoofbeats approaching
reading.explain: The text describes a sudden 'topot' (hoofbeat sound) that freezes her blood with fear, as Onegin arrives.

reading.ru: В саду служанки на грядах сбирали ягоды в кустах, и хором по наказу пели.
reading.question: What are the maidservants doing in the garden while Tatiana waits for Onegin?
options: Gathering berries in the bushes while singing in chorus, as instructed
reading.correct: Gathering berries in the bushes while singing in chorus, as instructed
reading.explain: The text says the maidservants gathered berries among the bushes and sang in chorus as ordered (so they would not eat the berries secretly).
